text:
oliver: Heads up—SIEM alert: surge of KMS decrypt failures starting ~08:12 UTC. Looks like many identical errors from svc-account:svc-rotator. Anyone digging?
sec-bot: AUTO ALERT: Rule 2043 triggered: KMS.Decrypt.Failure count=820 in 5m from 10.0.3.0/24, severity=high, fingerprint=KMS_DECRYPT_403
mar ia: I see. Quick check — did we push any RBAC changes for KMS or KMS key policy?
sara: No KMS policy changes in the last 24h. Audit shows a batch job (svc-rotator v2.1) started at 08:10 and performed many decrypt calls. Sample log:
```
2026-03-15T08:10:23Z svc-rotator[pid=3214] INFO attempt=1 svc=svc-rotator action=decrypt key=my-app-key err=PermissionDenied
2026-03-15T08:10:24Z svc-rotator[pid=3214] INFO attempt=2 svc=svc-rotator action=decrypt key=my-app-key err=PermissionDenied
2026-03-15T08:10:25Z svc-rotator[pid=3214] INFO attempt=3 svc=svc-rotator action=decrypt key=my-app-key err=PermissionDenied
```
oliver: So it's a retry storm from the rotation job hitting the same 403 repeatedly and spiking the rule. We should suppress noise but also fix the root cause (why it's 403).
maria: Root cause theory: the job rotated its own service account recently and didn't pick up new IAM binding, so first decrypt attempts fail until a short propagation window. Meanwhile it retries aggressively.
gabe: For SIEM -> propose two changes: 1) dedupe by request resource+error within 2m (collapse repeated identical errors from same sa/key), 2) add a suppression for alerts where the only actor tag == svc-rotator and event_count < 200 in 10m (so we don't quiet genuine large attacks). Also add a metric to surface distinct error codes rather than raw count.
anna: I can open the SIEM rule PR. Will include: group_by: [service_account, key_id, error_code] aggregate: count window: 2m collapse_threshold: 5 suppression_whitelist: ["svc-rotator"] (but with cap).
sara: Also recommend changing job to exponential backoff + jitter and fail open after N attempts to avoid hitting KMS repeatedly. I'll file a PR on rotator with backoff and 10s jitter.
maria: Action items:
- anna: PR for SIEM rule changes (include dashboard tiles) — ETA 2 business days
- sara: PR for rotator backoff + audit tag that records attempt counts — ETA today EOD
- oliver: investigate why SA didn't have new binding/propagation delay; check k8s rollout and key management logs — ETA 4h
- gabe: update playbook (alert conditions + suppression notes) and add unit test for rule to avoid regressions — ETA 3 days
sec-bot: NOTE: incident created #INC-2026-042 in PagerDuty, severity=low (noise).
oliver: For immediate mitigation, can we temporarily mute rule 2043 for the service_account=svc-rotator for 1h while we push the backoff? Only if SIEM can still surface distinct actors.
gabe: We can add a suppression window flagged in the alert so ops knows it's muted. I don't love muting, but acceptable with comms.
maria: I'll approve a 1h scoped suppression. anna, add annotation in the rule PR to auto-add a muted tag when merged.
anna: On it. I'll also add a dashboard card: "KMS decrypt failures (top 20 actors)" + a separate series for distinct error types so we can spot real threats.
sara: Filed rotator PR: https://git.redwood/svc-rotator/pull/458 — adds exponential backoff (base=0.5s, max=30s), jitter, and emits metric rotator.decrypt_attempts with tag result=deny/ok.
oliver: Great. Once rotator PR is out and rule updated, we should run book review and post-incident note. Please add notes to the incident doc.
gabe: I'll draft the postmortem template focusing on detection tuning vs app resilience. Include TL;DR, timeline, root cause, mitigations, action owners.
maria: Closing note: this is a useful class of FP — retry storms from known maintenance jobs. We should add a short runbook entry: when large KMS spikes coincide with a deployment or rotation job, check service-account tag and throttle rule.
anna: PR opened for SIEM rule: https://siem.redwood/rules/2043/changes/789 — includes dedupe + suppression.
oliver: Thanks everyone. We'll sync after anna's PR is merged. :thumbsup:
